acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Nagas family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Hooded Adept, T3, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Four-Hand Script Specialist (Specialist) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two earth construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: First broad cobra hood, four arms, jeweled scale inlay along the spine, and silk sash create the decisive Specialist pivot.

Signature mechanic: Three-Glyph Coil: the upper hands reveal the broad cobra hood and place Start and End glyphs while the lower hands rotate one jeweled spine segment between them; crossing the segments out of order tightens the surrounding coil, but striking the hand holding the middle glyph breaks the rule.
battlefieldDuty: Qualitatively pivot the fight by using the first hood and second arm pair to reorder three marked coil segments into a temporary movement rule.
constructionDimensions: Tier-safe anatomy: T1–T2 retain no hood and two arms with mineral cuffs and segmented scale weights; T3–T5 retain hood and multiple arms with load-bearing stone inlay following existing hood ribs and arm bands.
Coil and temple construction gains fitted stone scutes, crystal hinges, sediment-filled gold channels, planted counterweights, and pale fracture seams that move along the currently loaded outer coil.
counterplay: Read the hand-owned order, cross Start-middle-End, or interrupt the lower hand carrying the middle glyph before the coil closes. Affinity signal: One segmented coil row settles against a crystal stop and turns chalk-white before a stone rite; break that stop or move inside the loaded outer curve.
forbiddenTreatments: Palette-only brown scales without mineral structure and altered load paths
Glow-only earth treatment without fitted stone, weight, and fractures
Invented early-tier hoods or extra arms to hold stone ornaments
Generic rock piles that obscure coil direction or temple mechanisms
identityInvariants: A humanoid torso rises from a long coiled serpent body; the T1–T2 forms have two arms and no hood, while hood and additional arms begin only at T3.
Emerald, jade, deep teal, gold, bronze, ivory, and jewel-toned scale patterns remain the family palette.
Scale, gold, gemstone inlay, silk sash, and temple stone remain separate readable materials rather than a seamless magical body.
Arm bands, gold scale bands, jeweled brow pieces, sacred script, and later hood crests communicate rank.
Coil direction, weapon-bearing hands, hood angle where present, and exposed scale seams preserve attack and counterplay readability.
telegraph: The first broad hood fans open, four hands separate into upper and lower pairs, and three jeweled scale inlays brighten in a readable sequence.
